title: A small unrelated merge to main does not force a full CI re-run of the batch
why: Your gripe, Oct 27 16:36 CDT (cmsg_01DoF7thf3iq2Srr1UsfXgh2JnNhZbLrApWKBF2VyEBa6t): insignificant merges cause fat CI runs. Since c97 (PR #659), merge.py refuses a batch head that lacks main's tip, so each small merge to main (#713, #717, #701 during the freeze) forced a full 50 to 60 minute re-run.
note: Options for the lane to weigh, against c97's reason (a batch is proven on the main it lands on): (a) merge.py accepts the old run when main's new commits touch none of the batch's files and none of the files its jobs read; (b) a GitHub merge queue, which tests the combined head once; (c) on a base move, re-run only the jobs whose inputs changed (c95 step 2's scoped runs). Triage's lean: (a) first, since it is small and keeps c97's proof wherever an overlap could break it; (c) arrives with c95. Red first on today's case: a records-only merge to main forcing a full re-run of an unrelated batch. Needs no answer. Port: no; merge.py lives in claude-settings. Doing: lane started Oct 27 CDT (orchestrator), branch c150-small-merge-rerun from main e0f9e2d, option (a): merge.py keeps the old green run only when main's new paths share none with the batch, turn on no CI job per .github/scripts/ci-scope.sh, and bin/ci-job gates --lint passes on the merge result; else today's refusal. Try 1 (74428e57): Opus review round 1 found DOC_SUITES, a hand list of suites that read docs, misses two; try 2 derives the set from gates.yml. Placed ahead of c82, after c95 (triage, Oct 27): the same CI cost, from the merge side.
